  <section class="resource-section" id="starter-packages" aria-labelledby="starter-title">
  <div class="resource-section__header">
  <p class="eyebrow">Working reflex</p>
  <h2 id="starter-title">Starter packages</h2>
  <p>A package is not just a line of code to copy: it is a dependency of your document. The useful reflex is to distinguish installation, loading and precise function calls.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="course-flow">
  <article class="flow-card">
  <span class="flow-number">1</span>
  <h3>Install once</h3>
  <p><code>install.packages("package_name")</code> installs the package on your computer.</p>
  </article>
  <article class="flow-card">
  <span class="flow-number">2</span>
  <h3>Load at the start</h3>
  <p><code>library(tidyverse)</code> makes functions available in the active R session.</p>
  </article>
  <article class="flow-card">
  <span class="flow-number">3</span>
  <h3>Call precisely</h3>
  <p><code>readr::read_csv()</code> uses a function without loading the whole package.</p>
  </article>
  <article class="flow-card">
  <span class="flow-number">4</span>
  <h3>Check rendering</h3>
  <p>A Quarto document must load every package it depends on inside the file itself.</p>
  </article>
  </div>
  </section>

  <section class="resource-section" id="package-errors" aria-labelledby="package-errors-title">
  <div class="resource-section__header">
  <p class="eyebrow">Troubleshooting</p>
  <h2 id="package-errors-title">When R cannot find a package or function</h2>
  <p>Most package errors come from one of the four situations below.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="resource-hub-grid">
  <article>
  <h3>Package not found</h3>
  <p>Install the package, then render the document again. Installation is done once per computer.</p>
  </article>
  <article>
  <h3>Function not found</h3>
  <p>Load the package with <code>library()</code> or call the function with <code>package::function()</code>.</p>
  </article>
  <article>
  <h3>Name conflict</h3>
  <p>Use an explicit call, such as <code>dplyr::filter()</code>, to tell R which function to use.</p>
  </article>
  <article>
  <h3>Quarto render failure</h3>
  <p>Add the required <code>library()</code> calls inside the <code>.qmd</code> file, not only in the Console.</p>
  </article>
  </div>
  </section>
</div>

```{r}
#| label: setup-packages
#| include: false

library(dplyr)
library(htmltools)
library(knitr)
library(purrr)
library(tibble)

html_text <- function(x) htmltools::htmlEscape(as.character(x))

package_logos <- c(
  dplyr = "../assets/img/packages/dplyr.png",
  ggplot2 = "../assets/img/packages/ggplot2.png",
  tidyverse = "../assets/img/packages/tidyverse.png"
)

package_initials <- function(name) {
  cleaned <- gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]", "", name)
  if (!nzchar(cleaned)) {
    return("R")
  }
  toupper(substr(cleaned, 1, min(3, nchar(cleaned))))
}

package_catalog <- tibble::tribble(

)

package_label <- function(id) {
  package_catalog |> filter(.data$id ==.env$id) |> pull(.data$name) |> first()
}

render_package_tags <- function(ids) {
  ids <- unlist(ids, use.names = FALSE)
  links <- purrr::map_chr(ids, function(id) {
  paste0("<a href=\"#", id, "\"><code>", html_text(package_label(id)), "</code></a>")
  })
  paste0("<div class=\"tag-list\"><p>", paste(links, collapse = "\n"), "</p></div>")
}

render_package_card <- function(row) {
  tag <- ifelse(is.na(row$url), "section", "a")
  href <- ifelse(is.na(row$url), "", paste0(' href="', row$url, '" target="_blank" rel="noopener"'))
  source_label <- ifelse(is.na(row$url), "Local documentation or to be specified", "External documentation")
  logo_path <- unname(package_logos[row$id])
  logo <- if (!is.na(logo_path)) {
    paste0(
      '<span class="package-logo"><img src="', logo_path, '" alt="Hexagonal logo of the ',
      html_text(row$name), ' package"></span>'
    )
  } else {
    paste0(
      '<span class="package-logo package-logo--fallback" aria-hidden="true">',
      html_text(package_initials(row$name)),
      '</span>'
    )
  }
  paste0(
  '<', tag, ' id="', row$id, '" class="package-card"', href, '>',
  logo,
  '<span>',
  '<h2>', html_text(row$name), '</h2>',
  '<span class="package-role">', html_text(row$role), '</span>',
  '<span class="package-source">', source_label, '</span>',
  '</span>',
  '</', tag, '>'
  )
}
```

## By module

The packages listed here are the ones that appear explicitly in the module activities. Some are working tools, while others mainly provide datasets for practice.

```{r}
#| label: packages-by-module
#| results: asis

for (index in seq_len(nrow(module_packages))) {
  row <- module_packages[index, ]
  cat("### ", row$module, " {#", row$module_id, "}\n\n", sep = "")
  cat(render_package_tags(row$packages[[1]]), "\n\n")
}
```

## Package library

The full library is here to help you find documentation. Cards with a logo are the central course packages; the other cards use the package initials.

```{r}
#| label: package-library
#| results: asis

cat("<div class=\"package-grid package-library-grid\">\n")
purrr::walk(seq_len(nrow(package_catalog)), ~ cat(render_package_card(package_catalog[.x, ]), "\n"))
cat("</div>\n")
```
